references.text: The psalm describes how God led His people with His arm, the children of Jacob and Joseph, reflecting the theme of God's guidance of His people.
Describes how God led His people out like a flock and guided them safely to His holy land and His holy mountain.
Refers to God's deliverance of Israel at the Red Sea and how He saved them from the hand of the enemy, with reference to גָּאַל (redemption).
Isaiah mentions how the Lord led His people through the depths with His glorious arm and brought them safely to their destination.
Uses the word גָּאַל to describe how the Lord redeemed Israel from Egypt with a strong hand.
Asks God to remember His congregation, which He purchased in times of old, and Mount Zion where He dwelt—His holy dwelling (נְוֵה קָדְשֶׁךָ).
God promises to redeem (גָּאַל) Israel with an outstretched arm, which is linked to the redemption mentioned in 15:13.
David sings about how the Lord leads him on paths of righteousness (נָחָה), reflecting the guidance found in Exodus 15:13.
Peter writes about being redeemed (ἐλυτρώθητε) with Christ's precious blood, which is the New Testament fulfillment of the גָּאַל theme.
Paul writes that Christ gave Himself to redeem us (λυτρώσηται), connecting to the redemption in Exodus.
Both verses highlight God's sovereign guidance from liberation to the establishment of a nation in the promised land.
Nehemiah confirms and expands on the 'redemption' with great power as the basis for the people being God's possession.
Deuteronomy uses nearly identical language to confirm that the exodus was the result of God's power, not the people's own strength.
Habakkuk relives the exodus as a saving event where God crushes the enemy to rescue His people.
The psalm complements the story of the exodus by describing the people's joyful response to God's guidance.
Isaiah interprets the Exodus leadership as a picture of God's Spirit's eternal guidance to give the people rest.
The number 14 shows that the same 'great mercy' that led the people out is also the basis for their forgiveness during the journey.
Solomon's prayer confirms that the people are God's possession because He brought them out of Egypt with great power.
